concepts.name: Coal: Classification and Rank Hierarchy
key_dimensions: Rank order from peat → lignite → bituminous → anthracite and carbon content differences
UPSC trap: Lignite called 'brown coal' vs bituminous as 'thermal coal' — conflation errors
Coking coal vs non-coking coal distinction and their industrial applications
Why anthracite is rare in India despite being highest rank — geological age factor

concepts.name: Gondwana Coalfields vs Tertiary Coalfields of India
key_dimensions: Gondwana fields: age (~250 MYA), location (Damodar, Mahanadi, Son-Narmada belts), quality (bituminous/coking)
Tertiary fields: age (~15–60 MYA), location (Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal, J&K), quality (lignite/sub-bituminous)
UPSC trap: Neyveli lignite is Tertiary but located in Tamil Nadu (not NE India) — exception to spatial pattern
Gondwana coalfields account for ~98% of India's total coal reserves — significance for energy security

concepts.name: Major Coalfield Regions and Their River Basin Associations
key_dimensions: Damodar Valley: Jharia (only coking coal source), Raniganj, Bokaro — strategic importance
Son-Narmada belt: Singrauli, Umaria, Johilla coalfields in MP
Mahanadi belt: IB Valley, Talcher (Odisha) — largest reserves in any single state
UPSC trap: Distinguishing which coalfield lies in which state — Raniganj straddles WB/Jharkhand

concepts.name: Petroleum: Sedimentary Basin Distribution in India
key_dimensions: Mumbai High (offshore) — largest producing field, accounts for majority of domestic crude output
Assam fields: Digboi (oldest), Naharkatiya, Moran — onshore, Brahmaputra basin association
Krishna-Godavari basin and Cauvery basin — emerging/newer exploration zones
UPSC trap: Not all sedimentary basins are petroliferous — distinction between identified, explored, and producing basins

concepts.name: Natural Gas: Types, Distribution and NELP Framework
key_dimensions: Associated gas vs non-associated gas — occurrence relative to crude oil deposits
KG-D6 block (Reliance) — significance, production decline controversy, policy implications
HBJ Pipeline (Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur) — first major gas grid, trunk pipeline network
NELP (New Exploration Licensing Policy) vs HELP (Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy) — shift to revenue sharing model

concepts.name: Refinery Distribution and Strategic Significance in India
key_dimensions: India as a net exporter of petroleum products despite being a net importer of crude oil — processing hub paradox
Coastal vs inland refineries: Jamnagar (world's largest), Koyali, Mathura, Panipat
UPSC trap: Digboi refinery — oldest in Asia (not just India), located in Assam
Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR): Visakhapatnam, Mangalore, Padur — purpose and capacity

concepts.name: Thermal Power: Plant Types and Efficiency Parameters
key_dimensions: Super-critical vs ultra-super-critical vs sub-critical technology — efficiency and emission differences
Pit-head vs load-centre power plants — locational logic and transmission cost trade-offs
PLF (Plant Load Factor) as efficiency metric — India's declining PLF trend and stranded asset concern
UPSC trap: Combined Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT) plants use gas but are 'thermal' — classification overlap

concepts.name: Hydropower: Potential vs Actual Development in India
key_dimensions: India's total hydro potential (~1,50,000 MW) vs actual installed capacity — utilization gap
Himalayan rivers vs Peninsular rivers: different topography, run-of-river vs storage-based projects
UPSC trap: Small hydro (up to 25 MW) classified under renewable energy, not conventional hydro — policy boundary
Environmental concerns: sedimentation, seismic risk, forest submergence — Tehri Dam controversy

concepts.name: Major Hydroelectric Projects: Inter-State and International Dimensions
key_dimensions: Inter-state disputes: Cauvery, Krishna, Narmada (Sardar Sarovar) — tribunal awards and hydropower allocation
Transboundary projects: Indus Waters Treaty implications for Baglihar, Kishanganga dams
Run-of-river projects in NE India: Subansiri, Dibang — ecological and downstream flooding concerns
UPSC trap: Bhakra-Nangal — two separate dams on Sutlej; Bhakra is the dam, Nangal is the barrage downstream

concepts.name: Nuclear Energy: Fuel Cycle and India's Three-Stage Programme
key_dimensions: Stage 1: PHWRs using natural uranium; Stage 2: FBRs using plutonium; Stage 3: Thorium-based reactors
India's strategic logic — limited uranium but world's largest thorium reserves (Kerala, Jharkhand beaches)
UPSC trap: Uranium deposits at Jaduguda (Jharkhand), NOT in Rajasthan; monazite (thorium source) in coastal placers
Civilian vs military nuclear programme distinction — separation plan under Indo-US nuclear deal (123 Agreement)

concepts.name: Nuclear Power Plants: Location Logic and Reactor Types
key_dimensions: Coastal siting preference for large reactors — water cooling requirement (Kudankulam, Tarapur, Kaiga)
Reactor type mapping: PHWRs (NPCIL domestic), VVERs (Kudankulam — Russian), BWRs (Tarapur — American)
UPSC trap: Rawatbhata (Rajasthan) is inland nuclear plant on Chambal river — exception to coastal pattern
Installed nuclear capacity share in India's electricity mix (~3%) — significance despite high strategic profile

concepts.name: Coal India Limited (CIL): Structure, Subsidiaries and Market Dominance
key_dimensions: CIL as a Maharatna PSU controlling ~80% of India's coal production — monopoly concern
Subsidiary mapping: ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL, MCL, NEC — state-wise coverage
UPSC trap: Singareni Collieries (SCCL) is NOT a CIL subsidiary — it is a joint venture of GoI and Telangana govt
Commercial coal mining policy (2020): end of CIL's monopoly, 50+ blocks auctioned to private players

concepts.name: Energy Intensity and India's Energy Security Framework
key_dimensions: Energy intensity = energy consumed per unit of GDP — India's declining trend as development parameter
Four pillars of energy security: availability, accessibility, affordability, acceptability
UPSC trap: India is 3rd largest energy consumer globally but ranks low in per-capita consumption — absolute vs per-capita distinction
Integrated Energy Policy (2006) vs National Energy Policy (draft 2017) — key shifts in targets and fuels

concepts.name: Coal Washeries and Beneficiation: Environmental and Efficiency Dimension
key_dimensions: Coal beneficiation reduces ash content — India's coal has high ash (30–45%) compared to global average
Mandatory washing for power plants located >500 km from pithead — regulatory provision
UPSC trap: Washed coal improves calorific value and reduces fly ash, but washery rejects create slurry pollution
Link to PM2.5 and air quality — coal burning in thermal plants and brick kilns as pollution sources

concepts.name: Petroleum Pricing and Subsidy Architecture in India
key_dimensions: Administered Price Mechanism (APM) dismantling — petrol deregulated (2010), diesel (2014), LPG/kerosene still subsidised
DBTL (Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG) — Pahal scheme, world's largest DBT programme in energy
UPSC trap: Under-recoveries ≠ losses — under-recovery is the difference between market price and selling price, not accounting loss
Strategic petroleum reserve vs buffer stock — purpose distinction and India's 9.5 days of import cover

concepts.name: Coalbed Methane (CBM) and Coal Mine Methane (CMM): Emerging Conventional Gas
key_dimensions: CBM extracted from unmineable coal seams; CMM extracted as by-product during coal mining — source distinction
India's CBM potential concentrated in Damodar Valley, Sohagpur, Raniganj blocks
UPSC trap: CBM is classified under natural gas/conventional hydrocarbon in India's policy, unlike shale gas (unconventional)
Greenhouse gas dimension — methane from coal mines as fugitive emission; CMM capture as mitigation strategy

concepts.name: Electricity Transmission Grid: National Grid Integration and Frequency Zones
key_dimensions: Five regional grids (NR, SR, ER, WR, NER) integrated into ONE National Grid by 2013 — synchronization milestone
UPSC trap: Southern grid was last to join national grid (2013) due to different frequency (49.5 Hz vs 50 Hz standard)
HVDC vs HVAC transmission lines — HVDC used for long-distance bulk power (Rihand-Delhi, Vindhyachal)
Power Grid Corporation of India (PGCIL) — Central Transmission Utility role, not generation

concepts.name: Imported Coal Dependency and Port Infrastructure Linkage
key_dimensions: India imports coking coal (mainly from Australia) due to domestic shortage — strategic vulnerability
Thermal coal imports from Indonesia, South Africa — competitiveness vs domestic coal
UPSC trap: Despite being 4th largest coal reserve country, India is also among top 3 coal importers — reserve vs quality paradox
Dedicated coal port terminals: Paradip, Vishakhapatnam, Ennore, Mundra — coastal power plant strategy

concepts.name: Hydro-Thermal Mix and Load Balancing in India's Power Sector
key_dimensions: Ideal hydro-thermal mix considered 40:60 — India's current ratio skewed toward thermal (~70%+ thermal)
Hydro as peaking power vs thermal as base load — operational complementarity
UPSC trap: Pumped storage hydro acts as both generation and storage — blurs conventional vs storage boundary
Seasonal mismatch of hydro availability (monsoon peak) vs demand peak (summer) — grid management challenge

concepts.name: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh: Mineral-Energy Resource Concentration vs Development Paradox
key_dimensions: These three states hold majority of India's coal, iron ore, and bauxite — resource curse debate
Revenue sharing: District Mineral Foundation (DMF), PMKKKY scheme — community benefit mechanism
UPSC trap: Forest Rights Act vs mining clearance conflict — Schedule V areas, tribal displacement statistics
Left-wing extremism correlation with mineral-rich districts — governance and security dimension
